finding.claim: Strict-KEX (Terrapin) handshake message-order/sequence validation is dead code: validate_*_msg_strict_kex only runs when strict_kex && encrypted.is_none(), but strict_kex is only set at NEWKEYS in the same step that sets encrypted, so the guard is never true. The client side (client/mod.rs:1616-1619) is identical.
finding.source: Unauthenticated plaintext handshake packets (KEXINIT/KEX/NEWKEYS and IGNORE/DEBUG/UNIMPLEMENTED) sent before NEWKEYS, e.g. by an on-path attacker.
finding.sink: validate_client_msg_strict_kex / validate_server_msg_strict_kex (msg.rs:118-148), intended to reject non-conforming messages under strict KEX with strict_kex_violation.

trace.note: IGNORE/DEBUG/UNIMPLEMENTED silently returned before any strict check
strict_kex only set in KexProgress::Done, i.e. at NEWKEYS
encrypted() sets encrypted and strict_kex together at initial NEWKEYS (line 175)
seqno reset to 0 after strict NEWKEYS (mitigates sequence shift)
client has the same dead guard

finding.guards_checked: Strict flag negotiation is correct (negotiation.rs:245-261, 347). Post-NEWKEYS seqno reset is applied on both sides (server/mod.rs:1206-1208, client/mod.rs:1700-1702). IGNORE/DEBUG drop is intentional. Exploit impact beyond the missing disconnect is NOT established: I did not trace which non-IGNORE messages injected before NEWKEYS are processed by reply(). Treat as plausible, low severity, needs owner review.
